record.paper_title: Billiard Dynamics: A Survey with the Emphasis on Open Problems
record.original_question: Assume that for a dispersive billiard table Y the limit h = lim_{n→∞} (log f_Y(n))/n exists, where f_Y(n) counts periodic orbits of period at most n. Is this growth-rate constant h equal to the topological entropy of the billiard map?

evidence.quote: Problem 6. If the limit in equation (2.2) does exist, is h the topological entropy of the billiard map?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let Y be a dispersing (Sinai) billiard table: a compact connected region in the plane (or on the two-torus) whose boundary consists of finitely many smooth strictly convex arcs (curved so that the billiard flow is hyperbolic), and consider the associated billiard map T_Y on the cross-section of unit tangent vectors based at the boundary, defined by elastic reflection.

For each integer n ≥ 1, let f_Y(n) denote the number of periodic orbits of T_Y of period at most n. Assume that the limit
   h := lim_{n→∞} (log f_Y(n)) / n
exists in [0, ∞].

Question: Is h necessarily equal to the topological entropy h_top(T_Y) of the billiard map?
artifact.status_search_result: The equality between the exponential growth rate of periodic orbits and topological entropy for dispersing billiards is known to be subtle: Burago–Ferleger-type results give finite topological entropy and at-most-exponential growth of periodic orbits for semi-dispersing billiards, and lower bounds via topological entropy are known for hyperbolic 2D billiards, but the precise equality (and even the existence of the limit) is stated as an open problem in surveys on billiard dynamics. No published resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Topological Entropy Of Semi-Dispersing Billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Burago–Ferleger estimates establish finiteness of topological entropy and no more than exponential growth of periodic trajectories for non-degenerate semi-dispersing billiards.
status_evidence.claim: Topological entropy is finite and periodic orbit growth is at most exponential, but equality with the growth rate is not asserted.

status_evidence.title: Topological entropy and periodic points of two-dimensional hyperbolic billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Lower bounds for the number of periodic points of hyperbolic planar billiards via topological entropy.
status_evidence.claim: Inequalities relating periodic-orbit counts and topological entropy are known, but the question of equality of growth-rate constant with h_top is not settled.

status_evidence.title: Topological Entropy and Pressure for Finite Horizon Sinai Billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Recent advances on topological entropy and pressure for finite-horizon Sinai billiards.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research; relation to periodic orbit growth rate not stated as resolved.
